$comment: Staleness policy. Data, not code: changing a threshold is an edit to this file and needs no review of the script. Two windows bind every record. A class window (classes[confidence].days) says how fast a rung rots. A topic window (topics[<topic>].verified_after_days) says how fast a market rots. The shorter of the two is the record's limit, because it is the conservative one and it is checkable. evidence_after_days is a third, independent rule about one cited source, and it is applied to the oldest evidence row.

default.why: A record in a topic with no entry here is a topic nobody has priced. A quarter is the loose default and the gate prints it whenever it is used.

measured.why: The host still exists and the path still works. A measurement is the most durable rung and still not permanent.

documented.why: A vendor page changes without notice. The ladder allows 90 days for a protocol fact and 30 for a price or a quota; a record cannot say which kind it is, so the shorter binds, which is the conservative direction.

reported.why: A forum post describes a moment, and the operator may have fixed it.

inferred.why: The inference is only as fresh as its oldest premise.

unverified.why: The point of the label is that it gets checked.

storage.why: Prices and per-object caps move monthly; the seed needed ten waves in a year.

netdisk-pan.why: Public instances appear and vanish in weeks, and per-instance policy is set by whoever runs it that month.

compute.why: Free tiers are withdrawn without notice and sandbox reaping policies change.

coding-subs.why: Subscription price, included model and quota are the most volatile numbers in the corpus.

inference.why: Guest endpoints close and free tiers are rate-limited out of existence. The class window for a reported endpoint is 14 days and it binds; that is the honest number, not this one.

crawler-scraper.why: Provider catalogues are stable; their free allowances are not.

egress.why: Tunnel and CDN terms are contractual and slow-moving; IP ranges move faster.

email.why: SMTP limits are stable; free-sender allowances are not.

databases-kv.why: Free-tier row and connection caps change with each pricing revision.

domains-dns.why: Registrar pricing and TLD availability move on an annual cycle.

ci-cd-runners.why: Runner minutes and artifact retention are the two numbers that decide it, and both are revised.

debrid.why: Multi-hoster prices, host coverage and free tiers move monthly, and public instances vanish without notice. The class window for a reported figure is 14 days and it binds.

ip-proxy.why: Exit identity is the fastest-rotting fact in this corpus: a proxy vendor is re-registered, a prefix is re-announced, and a VPN moves its exits without announcement. Free proxy lists decay in minutes, so a list-derived record is reported at best.

dev-services.why: Monitoring, analytics, job, queue and authentication free tiers are revised with each pricing page change, about as often as compute free tiers. Set by the operator ruling of 2026-10-28 (issue #31).

data-apis.why: Free call quotas and rate limits of data APIs change with pricing revisions; bulk dumps and their licences move more slowly. Set by the operator ruling of 2026-10-28 (issue #43).

severity.$comment: Which condition fails the gate. A record is past its policy when any test below fires. 'bulk_touch' is the one that catches verified_at moving without the evidence moving with it, and it is the lie METHODOLOGY.md section 10.1 forbids by name. The 'bands' above are a reporting scale only: nothing gates on them, because a band is a description of age and the limit is the decision. An earlier version of this file carried a 'fail_on_bucket' list that no code read, which is the defect this repository refuses in records and should refuse in its own config.
